issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes the bound with exponent $2+1/\mathsf{r}$, where $\mathsf{r}\in(2n/(n+2),2]$ by Proposition prop:states_y-yt and $\mathsf{r}>n/2$ is needed for the embedding $\mathbf{W}^{2,\mathsf{r}}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{W}^{1,\mathsf{p}}$. Solving $2+1/\mathsf{r}-\tilde\delta=1+1/\gamma$ gives $\gamma=\mathsf{r}/(\mathsf{r}+1-\tilde\delta\mathsf{r})\le 2/3$, so the displayed relation produces at most $\gamma\in(n/(n+2),2/3]$; the remaining range $\gamma\in(2/3,1]$ is not justified by the analysis given. It is obtainable only by an additional absorption step (from $\lesssim\|\hat{\mathbf{u}}-\mathbf{u}\|_{\mathbf{L}^1}^{2+1/\mathsf{r}}$ with $2+1/\mathsf{r}\ge 1+1/\gamma$, use $\|\hat{\mathbf{u}}-\mathbf{u}\|_{\mathbf{L}^1}\le\delta<1$ to absorb the excess power into $\varepsilon$), which is missing. The lemma's conclusion is correct on the full stated range.

failure_location.quote: A straightforward analysis reveals that $2 + \frac{1}{\mathsf{r}} - \tilde{\delta} = 1 + \frac{1}{\gamma}$ with $\gamma \in (n/(n + 2), 1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Append the absorption argument: for $\gamma>2/3$ take $\mathsf{r}=2$ (exponent $5/2\ge 1+1/\gamma$) and use $\|\hat{\mathbf{u}}-\mathbf{u}\|_{\mathbf{L}^1}\le\delta<1$ to absorb the excess power into the constant $\varepsilon$; for $\gamma\le 2/3$ the displayed relation with $\mathsf{r}=\gamma/(1-\gamma)$ already works.
issues.overall_effect: No conclusion changes; the full range $\gamma\in(n/(n+2),1]$ of the lemma is correct, but the displayed analysis as written justifies only $\gamma\le 2/3$, leaving $(2/3,1]$ unsupported by the proof given.
issues.title: Exponent matching in lemma:sec_order as written covers only gamma <= 2/3, not the full stated range
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is true on the full stated range; only the final exponent-matching sentence is incomplete, and the missing step is a one-line absorption argument (routine local completion) with no loss of any claim or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h \to \bar{\mathbf{u}}$ when $h\to0$, we take $h$ sufficiently small such that we can use the growth condition \eqref{controlgrowth} in combination with the estimate
Then, there exists $h_{*} > 0$ such that for all $h \in (0,h_{*})$ the semidiscrete problem has a solution $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}$.
Then, there exists a sequence $\{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}\}_{h>0}$ of local minima of the semidiscrete problem such that $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}\to \bar{\mathbf{u}}$ in $\mathbf{L}^{1}(\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof explicitly uses $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h\to\bar{\mathbf{u}}$: to apply the growth condition (Assumption sufficientcon) and Lemma lemma:sec_order (which needs $\mathbf{u}_\theta\in\mathcal{O}(\bar{\mathbf{u}})$), to have $\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h}$ regular, and to have $\|\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h}-\bar{\mathbf{y}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\lesssim h^2$. But Theorem thm:exist_and_conv_sol_var, which supplies $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h$, asserts only existence; convergence $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h\to\bar{\mathbf{u}}$ in $\mathbf{L}^1$ is established in Theorem thm:added-2 only under the additional strict-local-minimum assumption and for a suitable sequence. Hence the theorem as stated lacks a hypothesis its proof essentially needs (discrete solutions need not be unique or convergent).

issues.failure_explanation:
The state error $\mathbf{e}=\mathbf{y}_{ ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h}- ar{\mathbf{y}}_h$ satisfies $\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\lesssim h^2$ but only $\|
abla\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\lesssim h$ in general: the control is merely in $\mathbf{L}^2$ on a convex polyhedron, so the velocity has only $\mathbf{H}^2$ regularity, and the $P_2$-$P_1$ $H^1$-error is $O(h)$ (sharp for $\mathbf{H}^2\setminus\mathbf{H}^3$ solutions). Splitting $\mathbf{e}$ into interpolation and discrete parts and using inverse estimates yields $\|
abla\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{6/5}}\lesssim h$, and $\|
abla\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{6/5}}\ge|\Omega|^{-1/6}\|
abla\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}$, so the claimed $h^2$ bound is false in general. Consequently, for $n=3$ the argument gives $\|
abla(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h- ar{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\lesssim h$ and $\| ar{\mathbf{u}}- ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^1}^{1/\gamma}\lesssim h|\log h|+h^{-1/2}\cdot h=h|\log h|+h^{1/2}$, i.e. only $\| ar{\mathbf{u}}- ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^1}\lesssim h^{\gamma/2}$ — the advertised $(h|\log h|)^\gamma$ 3D rate is unsupported as written (the 2D case is unaffected, since the 2D inverse estimate is only logarithmic). The rate is recovered by a contained reestimate: the antisymmetry $b(\mathbf{w}_h;\mathbf{e},\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h)=-b(\mathbf{w}_h;\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h,\mathbf{e})$ and the Gagliardo–Nirenberg bound $\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^3}\lesssim\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}^{1/2}\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{H}^1}^{1/2}\lesssim h^{3/2}$ give $\|b(\cdot;\mathbf{e},\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{H}^{-1}}\lesssim h^{3/2}$, hence $\|
abla(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h- ar{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\lesssim h^{3/2}$ and $h^{-1/2}\cdot h^{3/2}=h\lesssim h|\log h|$.

failure_location.quote: Finally, using interpolation and inverse estimates, and estimate $\|\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_{h}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{2}(\Omega)} \lesssim h^{2}$, we obtain $\|\nabla(\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_{h})\|_{\mathbf{L}^{\frac{6}{5}}(\Omega)} \lesssim h^{2}$.

Replace the false bound $\|
abla(\mathbf{y}_{ ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h}- ar{\mathbf{y}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^{6/5}}\lesssim h^2$ by the antisymmetry-based estimate $\|b(\cdot;\mathbf{y}_{ ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h}- ar{\mathbf{y}}_h,\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{H}^{-1}}\lesssim\|
abla\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\|\mathbf{y}_{ ar{ oldsymbol{u}}_h}- ar{\mathbf{y}}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^3}\lesssim h^{3/2}$ (using $\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^3}\lesssim\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}^{1/2}\|\mathbf{e}\|_{\mathbf{H}^1}^{1/2}$), giving $\|
abla(\hat{\mathbf{z}}_h- ar{\mathbf{z}}_h)\|_{\mathbf{L}^2}\lesssim h^{3/2}$ and preserving the 3D rate $(h|\log h|)^\gamma$; alternatively accept the degraded 3D rate $h^{\gamma/2}$.
issues.overall_effect: In 3D the control error rate degrades from the advertised $(h|\log h|)^\gamma$ to $h^{\gamma/2}$ along the given proof, and cor:added-1's 3D state rate degrades likewise; the 2D results are unaffected. With the antisymmetry-based reestimate the advertised 3D rate is restored.
issues.title: False h^2 bound for the L^{6/5}-gradient of the state error breaks the advertised 3D rate
issues.why_classification: As written the proof contains a false estimate and the 3D rate collapses from $(h|\log h|)^\gamma$ to $h^{\gamma/2}$; a contained reestimate with tools already used in the paper (antisymmetry of b and Sobolev interpolation) restores the advertised rate, so no new proof architecture or major loss is needed, but the repair goes beyond a local patch.
